tools.name: get_review
tools.description: Fetch a Cobalt Capture review by its share link or slug. Returns the reviewer's notes as text AND each annotated screenshot as an image, so you can see exactly what was marked and what to change.

tools.name: create_review
tools.description: Start a new Cobalt Capture review and get a handle for filling it in. Use this to compile the findings of any site study — a usability pass, a pricing teardown, a positioning audit, a QA run — into one shareable, durable report with real screenshots. Works from any client, chat assistants included:

tools.name: add_screenshot
tools.description: Append one screenshot, with an optional title and note, to the end of a review. The image is stored in Cobalt and shown in the review. Three ways to supply it: `page_url`, a public page that Cobalt renders in a headless browser (`viewport` 'desktop' at 1280px or 'mobile' at 390px, `full_page` for th

tools.name: replace_screenshot
tools.description: Overwrite one existing screenshot in a review with a new capture, in the same position. Destructive: the old image and any pins or annotations on it are removed and cannot be recovered; the title and comment change only if new ones are passed. Works on screenshots only, not notes. Takes the same cap

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Append a free-standing text note (not tied to a screenshot) to a review created by create_review. Use for context, steps taken, or a summary of findings between screenshots.

tools.name: update_review
tools.description: Set or replace a review's summary and/or title. The summary is shown at the top of the review, above every screenshot and note. Replaces any existing summary or title.

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Return the full text of a Cobalt study playbook: a step-by-step method for a kind of product review that ends in a shareable Cobalt review. Available: 'pricing_teardown' (can a buyer tell what they would pay and which tier fits; public pages only); 'website_teardown' (what each key page leads with a

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the studies Cobalt Capture has published on well-known products: pricing teardowns, positioning audits, and head-to-head comparisons (for example Canva pricing, Spotify vs Apple Music). Returns matching studies as {id, title, url}; pass an id to fetch for the full text. It does NOT search pri

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full text of a Cobalt study by the id search returned, or of any Cobalt review by its URL (/r/<slug>) or slug. Returns text: findings, prices, the comparison matrix, and the underlying review's notes with links to its screenshots. Use get_review instead when you need to see the screenshots

tools.name: create_inbox
tools.description: Create a temporary email inbox for testing the signup or email flow of a product the user owns or is authorised to test, within that product's terms. Returns an `address` to enter in the product's form and an `inbox_token` for reading it with check_inbox. Each inbox expires 24 hours after it is crea

tools.name: check_inbox
tools.description: Read mail delivered to an inbox from create_inbox, newest first, for example a verification code or confirmation link from the signup email of the product being tested. Requires the inbox_token, so only whoever created the inbox can read it. Returns immediately; mail usually arrives within seconds,

tools.name: email_review
tools.description: Email a link to a review to the person who ran the study. Sends only to an address that belongs to a verified Cobalt account (other addresses are refused, which keeps the tool from being used to send unsolicited mail). The email contains only the review link, never text supplied in the call.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "add_screenshot" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_review, create_review, get_playbook, search, fetch, check_inbox · Private data: search · Public sink: get_review, create_review, add_screenshot, create_inbox, check_inbox, email_review · Destructive: create_review, replace_screenshot, get_playbook, check_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_review, create_review, get_playbook, search, fetch, check_inbox · Private data: search · Public sink: get_review, create_review, add_screenshot, create_inbox, check_inbox, email_review · Destructive: create_review, replace_screenshot, get_playbook, check_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
